# TEST ONLY: deterministic recording-security corpus

This corpus exercises PR41's resource gates against ordinary, boundary and
intentionally malformed asciicast input. It is **not** a collection to open in an
unprotected terminal player. Do not upload generated boundary files to a real
WordPress site, serve them publicly, or commit expanded large payloads.

Only small, readable `.cast` files are checked in. Large cases are compact
literal/repeat recipes materialized one at a time in temporary storage. The
largest possible file is **32 MiB + 1 byte**. There is no arbitrary size argument,
unbounded fuzz loop, network request, remote command, or production-code import
in the generator. The ordinary plugin package excludes the `tests` directory.

## Provenance and reproducibility

- `official-v1.cast`, `official-v2.cast`, and `official-v3.cast` are unmodified
  **native recordings** from pinned official CLI versions. Legacy CLI 1.4.0
  produced v1; CLI 3.0.1 produced v2 and v3. Their actual timestamps and PTY delays
  remain intact. See [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) and `provenance.json` for
  official source URLs, verified package hashes, commands and capture hashes.
- `seeded-v*-valid.cast` are explicitly **normalized derivatives**, not raw CLI
  output. They retain the captured output text and the recorded format/dimension
  envelope, remove nondeterministic metadata, add seeded harmless UTF-8 output,
  and use fixed visible START/SEEK/END frames across a 12-second timeline. v2
  stores absolute time; v1/v3 store matching intervals. These are the interactive
  playback/seek controls.
- Resource-boundary derivatives mutate one documented resource purpose. JSONL
  byte and line fillers are actual output events, not padding comments. Wide
  metadata, deep metadata and large valid grids are valid-format resource-unsafe
  cases; they must fail the intended policy rather than generic JSON syntax.
- Blank/comment/indented lines, zero header dimensions and duplicate keys are
  marked `upstream-compatible`, independently of strict format provenance.
- `malformed-v*` cases deliberately contain broken JSON and are labeled
  `intentionally-malformed`.

`recipes.mjs` uses real unsigned xorshift32 (`<<13`, `>>>17`, `<<5`) with the
single allowed seed `0x41c0ffee` (1103167470). Randomized output chunks, text and
bounded timings are deterministic. Equivalent purposes use all three formats
where their semantics permit it. v1 has a whole-document 2 MiB budget and no
marker/resize event types; those JSONL-only purposes apply to v2/v3. A fresh
official PTY recording is not byte-identical; the checked-in raw captures are
immutable, independently hash-pinned anchors, not regenerated during tests.

## Commands

Run from the repository root using the project's supported Node version:

```sh
# List bounded, known case IDs, sizes and expected results.
node tests/fixtures/security/generate.mjs --list

# Compare deterministic recipes to the golden manifest and verify every hash.
node tests/fixtures/security/generate.mjs --verify

# Write exactly one known file to a new OS temporary directory.
node tests/fixtures/security/generate.mjs --case markers-v2-over

# Independent corpus metrics plus actual production loader and player Core.
node --test tests/js/security-fixtures.test.js tests/js/security-loader-fixtures.test.js

# All JavaScript checks, including both corpus suites.
npm test

# Native PHP 7.4+; needs neither Node nor the asciinema CLI.
php tests/php/run.php

# Real isolated WordPress/Chromium integration; see tests/e2e/README.md setup.
npx --no-install playwright test tests/e2e/security-fixtures.spec.js
```

The `--case` command prints the temporary path, byte count, SHA-256 and cleanup
directory. Delete that directory after inspection. Test consumers clean up their
own temporary files in `finally` blocks. Never replace the named case ID with a
user-controlled arbitrary size. Large samples must stay outside source control.

When intentionally changing a recipe, run `--refresh` and review the complete
manifest/hash/small-fixture diff, then rerun the checks above. This writes only
the manifest and tiny derivative files; it never rewrites official captures or
expands large cases into the repository. Provenance checks independently reject
a changed raw baseline even if someone refreshes the golden manifest.

## Shared cross-language contract

`manifest.json` has `schemaVersion: 1`, an independently pinned `policy`, seed,
and a `cases` array. Each case declares:

- `id`, `format`, `description`, `category`, `validity`, and `provenance`
- Exactly one `source.file` relative to this directory, or ordered
  `source.segments: [{ "text": "literal UTF-8", "repeat": positiveInteger }]`
- `bytes` and lowercase SHA-256 of the exact generated bytes
- `expected.accepted` and exact `expected.jsError` (null for accepted controls)
- Optional `boundary: {metric, limit, value}` and independent `metrics`
- `safePlayback: true` only for the six tiny official/seeded accepted controls
- Optional `playback` expectations for the normalized interactive controls

Concatenate the UTF-8 bytes of each literal repeated by its count in order. Do
not normalize newlines, strip BOMs, reserialize JSON, execute text, or shell out
to Node from PHP. The JavaScript reader verifies size and SHA-256 before use;
the PHP reader streams at most 64 KiB at a time to one temporary file and checks
the same identity before invoking the actual file/upload/sideload gates.

`expected.noDecodeAtOrAboveBytes` is a witness threshold for rejected JSON trees:
the decoder must not see any tree input that large. Small safe headers or tiny
version-discriminator scalar parses may still occur. Byte-over JSONL differs by
consumer: PHP rejects from file size before any decode, expressed by the stronger
`expected.phpNoDecodeAtOrAboveBytes: 1`; a browser stream must parse safe earlier
records before discovering the final byte, then cancel without handing the
recording to the player. This is not a claim that all streaming prefix parsing
can or should be avoided.

## Coverage map

| Purpose | Case IDs | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official provenance and real playback | `official-v{1,2,3}`, `seeded-v{1,2,3}-valid` | Same native output; normalized equivalent timelines |
| Zero/blank/multiline compatibility | `valid-v*-zero`, `valid-v{2,3}-filtered-lines`, `valid-v1-multiline-late-version` | Small actual files |
| Format discrimination | `valid-v1-escaped-version`, `valid-v1-duplicate-version`, `valid-v1-long-first-line`, `invalid-v2-duplicate-version-wide` | v1 limits cannot leak into v2 |
| Whole body bytes | `bytes-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 33,554,432 / 33,554,433 bytes |
| Legacy v1 bytes | `v1-bytes-{at,over}` | 2,097,152 / 2,097,153 bytes |
| JSONL bytes including LF | `line-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 262,144 / 262,145 bytes |
| Events | `events-v{1,2,3}-{at,over}` | 100,000 / 100,001 events |
| Physical JSONL work | `ignored-lines-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 100,000 / 100,001 lines; exactly one output event |
| Markers | `markers-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 1,000 / 1,001 markers |
| Header and late-resize axes | `dimensions-v*-{at,over}`, `late-resize-v{2,3}-dimensions-{at,over}` | 1,000 / 1,001 columns, otherwise safe |
| Header and late-resize cells | `cells-v*-{at,over}`, `late-resize-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 200×200 / 201×200; each axis remains valid |
| v1 scalar/key allocation | `tokens-v1-{at,over}` | 400,000 / 400,001 tokens |
| v1 container allocation | `containers-v1-{at,over}` | 100,016 / 100,017 containers |
| JSONL scalar/key allocation | `line-tokens-v{2,3}-{at,over}` | 20,000 / 20,001 tokens |
| Nesting | `depth-v{1,2,3}-{at,over}` | 15 / 16 container levels |
| Recording timeline | `timeline-v{1,2,3}-{at,over}` | 2,147,483,647 / 2,147,483,648 milliseconds |
| Relative timeline sum | `interval-timeline-v{1,3}-{at,over}` | Millisecond-order accumulation at / over the horizon |
| Time metadata | `duration-v*-{zero,at,over}`, `idle-limit-v*-{zero,at,over}` | Zero remains valid; inclusive horizon applies |
| Floating-point regressions | `time-v{1,3}-ms-rounding-over`, `time-v{1,3}-ms-sum-overflow`, `time-v2-output-nonprogress` | Valid JSON with unsafe upstream millisecond arithmetic |
| Intentional bad syntax | `malformed-v1-json`, `malformed-v{2,3}-event` | Stable invalid-result controls |

The cells-over value is 40,200, not an assertion that every integer cell count
has a valid integer grid. Event-only JSONL reaches the physical-line and event
caps together; the ignored-line pair independently isolates physical-line work.
There is no separate per-line cap on whole-document v1, and no JSONL-wide 400,000
token budget: those distinctions are explicit rather than false all-format
equivalence.

The corpus invariant suite independently parses tightly bounded test data to
measure structure, verify valid/malformed labels, pin exact boundary values,
and prove an unrelated limit is not masking the intended one. Only the six
`safePlayback` controls use ordinary real pinned player Core playback. Separate
tiny timestamp regressions use captured timers and bounded callbacks to verify
upstream numeric behavior without scheduling long waits or an unbounded loop.
Hostile/boundary recordings first exercise the production loader guard or PHP
upload validator.

The supported raw timeline is about 24.85 days. Browser playback conservatively
requires cumulative time divided by speed to fit the same signed timer ceiling;
at 0.01×, this permits about 5.97 hours of source time. Per-event gap checks alone
are insufficient because the player batches future output ahead of wall time.
The v1/v3 rounding witness specifically distinguishes summing milliseconds from
summing seconds before conversion; these two operations are not interchangeable.
Browser tests use the existing isolated WordPress setup and check visible errors
and recovery. Passing Node/PHP checks does not imply that a browser run occurred.

## Relationship to existing tests

Existing `hello.cast`, `replacement.cast`, `resize.cast`, `v1-pretty.cast`, and
`v3-comments.cast` remain the ordinary UI regression fixtures. Existing inline
small-limit unit tests remain useful for cancellation, option overrides, UTF-8
failures and timing edge cases. This corpus adds durable official provenance,
actual full-default at/over resource pairs, deterministic cross-language input,
decoder-order witnesses and a common source for upload and playback integration;
it does not replace those focused tests.
